I LOVE THIS GAME. The visuals are absolutely stunning, the story can keep you entertained for a lifetime (especially with all the 12 hour lore videos), and I think that the difficult is perfect. Majority of the bosses felt fun to fight, and I also like that you can pivot to other bosses or quests if you get stuck to then get stronger and finally beat them. That is something I feel is not really much shown in the Dark Souls games. Every time you play this game, there will always be something new that you discover. 
As I have played through this game more, I have come to enjoy one of the boss fights quite a lot. This being Fire Giant. It may be controversial, but I enjoy that fight. I love that it teaches you patience, and a lot of it. It will feel like you are fighting him for 20 minutes at a time, but it is needed. 

I will say that I did experience some performance issues in some areas of the game. But, it was never unplayable. Faraum Azula was the worst because of how much was going on. All be it, my PC is not very top of the line, but I also would not say that it is terrible either.

Incredible graphics. Amazing story telling. Challenging gameplay.

This might be top 3 best games of all time.

Sure, choosing any other class than one where you're fast and can dodge out of enemies attacks is useless. But when you get over that, it's an amazing game. 

The map is huge and there are so many side quests, there is never nothing to do. When I first got to the end of the game, I realized I had skipped one of the first sections of the game and had to go back, where even though I was too strong for the area, had a very good time exploring and getting new items. 

There are also many endings which makes it for a good game to re-play.

Now sure, the bosses are very hard. But that's where the fun comes in. This game made me a much calmer person in general. This might sound counter-intuitive to some, but to me, failing something dozens of times, thought me a valuable lesson about games never being that serious and also the precious lesson of not giving up.

I understand this game might not be for everybody, but if you're someone who's looking for a beautiful and challenging game, where you can choose your destiny and how you get there, this game is for you.

Never played a Fromsoft game before, and although I'm having fun, there are some issues I'm not seeing people talk about that I think should be mentioned. From most to least frustrating:
1. Consumables are awful. I hated them in Silksong, and I hate them here. I propose that they should not be permanently removed from your inventory after death unless you've made some permanent progress (beating a boss, touching a grace, etc.).
2. Abysmal keyboard controls. I've found a setup that works for me, but it's still very problematic. If I could bind multiple keys to the same action, or access the quick items without holding the interact button, it would be much better.
3. The 60 fps cap is stupid. Modders have fixed this issue. I've gotten used to it, but Fromsoft has no excuse.
4. Last, least, and most confusing, why is there no option for glyphs to automatically switch based on whether you're using a keyboard or controller? I also own a Legion Go, so if I want the glyphs to be accurate, I have to change a setting AND THE SETTING IS SYNCED BETWEEN DEVICES????

Overall, I like Elden Ring, and I'm interested to try Fromsofts other games, but these issues do not inspire confidence.

While its not the absolute "perfect" video game imo, it combines most of the best aspects of ds1-ds3, layering it over an utterly massive open world that actually rewards you for exploring rather than just being a checklist of go here do that. While you can absolutely full clear everything you can technically beat the game in as little as 9 bosses. The community might frown on using everything you acquire in the game to win but dont let that stop you from summoning or using spirit ashes for a boss - elden ring is designed to let you play it how you want to, just know it wont pull any punches if you decide to limit yourself to 1v1 every boss because of pride. Overall great game and the dlc is just as densely packed with content and further encourages the explore everything mindset, arguably far moreso than the base game as it basically has its own separate leveling system.
